title: Dynamic Interval Scheduling with Random Start and End Times: NP-hardness of the CDSRSE model (printed as Theorem 3.2)
author: Rui Gong, Alejandro Toriello
work: Dynamic Interval Scheduling with Random Start and End Times
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Theorem 3.2 (source0.tex lines 418--420), the NP-hardness of the CDSRSE scheduling model in which each task occupies one of two slots at random. It is delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 421--443 (23 lines, one adjacent proof environment, no gap and no deferral) and with the earlier NP-hardness statement the proof starts from. The proof is a genuine reduction argument: it constructs the instance with one long task and n singleton tasks, computes the effect of the model's deletion rule on the second task, identifies the resulting decision problem with the dynamic maximum stable set problem on a star graph, and concludes NP-hardness from the known hardness of that problem. The substantive step is the correctness of the identification of the two problems under the model's slot-occupation dynamics, which is not an unpacking of definitions. H2: a complete original research-paper theorem, moderately short, whose proof is a genuine reduction rather than a routine verification.
